CharterUP is transforming the $365 billion global group transportation and mobility market with an AI native platform that powers modern charter, shuttle, and emerging autonomous vehicle operations. Trusted by many Fortune 500 companies, CharterUP connects enterprises, institutions, and event organizers with thousands of vehicles nationwide, while increasingly serving as the operating system for large scale shuttle and transit programs across airports, campuses, industrial sites, and major events.

Through real time availability, transparent pricing, intelligent routing, and AI driven dispatch and optimization, CharterUP replaces a fragmented and opaque industry with automation, accountability, and scale.

Why Join Us

  • Innovative Impact: Be part of the team that's revolutionizing group travel, setting new standards in an industry overdue for change.
  • Growth Opportunities: As a hyper growth company and one of the fastest-growing companies recognized by Inc., there’s no better time to join our dynamic, growth-stage organization.
  • Driven Team: Collaborate with some of the most driven minds in tech, all while working in a remote-first environment with a tech hub in Austin, TX.
  • Funding and Stability: Our $60 million Series A funding was just the start—we’re poised for even greater expansion, and you can be part of this exciting journey. CharterUp has achieved this growth profitability and efficiently, ensuring long-term stability.

Title:Client Solutions Partner

Reports to:Sales Manager

Location: Remote

About the Role

This is an inbound and outbound sales role for people who are hungry to drive revenue, build repeat business, and own their results. It rewards individuals who thrive under pressure, act decisively, and operate with high urgency and precision. You will manage hundreds of customer interactions per week, build your own book of business, and ensure every booking experience reinforces CharterUP’s reputation for speed, reliability, and excellence.

As a Client Solutions Partner (CSP), you’ll be in the thick of the action, handling high volumes of inbound demand while chasing down the next opportunity before anyone else does. You’ll be responsible for both closing new customers and expanding recurring ones, managing a mini-portfolio of high-value accounts that rely on you as their trusted CharterUP contact. We’re looking for sharp, decisive, high-judgment sales athletes who can think fast, act faster, and refuse to settle for "good enough." You’ll be part of a team that executes with urgency, precision, and accountability every single day.

Responsibilities

  • Hit and exceed every metric. Own performance against conversion rates, revenue targets, outbound and inbound activity, repeat bookings, and overall account growth.
  • Manage a high volume of inbound leads while driving outbound reactivation and expansion efforts to capture repeat and new business.
  • Leverage CharterUP’s proprietary marketplace technology to create tailored, accurate trip quotes that minimize friction in the booking process.
  • Execute disciplined call patterns to maintain conversion velocity and follow-up consistency.
  • Build urgency, rapport, and trust in every interaction, closing decisively through confident communication and assumptive sales techniques.
  • Drive repeat business by identifying high-value accounts, expanding relationships over time, and turning one-time bookings into repeat relationships.
  • Apply call control, objection handling, and active listening to diagnose customer needs and drive efficient bookings.
  • Escalate only when needed, solve problems directly, and push through roadblocks to deliver outcomes.
  • Use sound judgment and data to decide where to focus for highest yield.
  • Detect and stop low-value activity early to protect revenue through commercial acumen.
  • Maintain complete accuracy in quoting, CRM updates, and call documentation, ensuring operational precision across systems including Salesforce, Outreach, G-Suite, Slack, and proprietary tools.
  • Collaborate with peers and leadership on post-mortems and performance reviews to refine tactics and improve execution.

Experience and Expertise

  • 3+ years of experience in sales, account management, or hybrid revenue roles, consistently exceeding performance goals.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage and grow a book of business, expanding spend, deepening relationships, and driving retention.
  • Proven success balancing high-volume inbound response with targeted outbound prospecting and account development.
  • Skilled in navigating multi-contact organizations and identifying new opportunities within existing accounts.
  • Expert communicator with mastery in objection handling, urgency creation, and assumptive closing across varied customer types.
  • Proficient in CRM and sales enablement tools (Salesforce, Outreach, G-Suite, Slack), ensuring disciplined follow-up and accurate documentation.
  • Analytical and data-driven, using performance metrics and conversion insights to guide activity and optimize revenue outcomes.
  • Comfortable owning end-to-end client relationships from quote generation to post-trip follow-up, feedback, and repeat engagement.
  • History of competitive achievement or performance-based success in athletics, startups, or other quota-driven environments.

What Defines You

Core Character

  • Extreme Ownership: You don’t wait for direction; you execute the mission.
  • Grit & Hunger: You outwork, outlast, and outthink everyone around you.
  • Self-Starter Energy: You see gaps, fill them, and move before others even notice.
  • Loyalty & Integrity: You keep your word, play for the team, and own your reputation.

What We Mean by Grit

  • Relentless follow-through: You pursue a clear yes or no; you don’t let deals stall.
  • High output as a habit: You work the plan daily and maintain volume during busy seasons.
  • Resilient under pressure: You handle rejection, ambiguity, and shifting priorities without losing momentum.
  • Competitive drive: You want to be at the top of the board and treat targets as non-negotiable.
  • Bias to action: You prefer testing and iterating over waiting for perfect information.

Cognitive & Decision Traits

  • High Intellect: You process fast, connect dots, and make the right call under pressure.
  • Analytical Judgment: You use data to make decisions, not noise.
  • Decisive Execution: You don’t overthink; you move with conviction.

Recruiting Process

Step 1: 30-minute call with Talent Acquisition
Step 2: 1-hour Video Call with a Hiring Manager
Step 3: 1-hour Video Call / Role Play Interview
Step 4: 30-minute Interview with CEO
Step 5: Offer and Background Check

Welcome aboard

Salary
$63,000—$120,000 USD

Global Benefits & Perks at CharterUP

We believe great people can live anywhere—and they deserve great benefits, too. While offerings may vary slightly by location, we prioritize hiring near our hubs in Austin, Atlanta, Miami, and Denver as we grow our global team.

  • Flexible Work Model: CharterUP operates as a remote-first company, with select roles requiring regular, in-office presence based on team and business needs. Role-specific expectations will be shared during the hiring process. U.S.-based employees may reside in any of our 19 approved states.
  • Comprehensive Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, mental health support, virtual care, gym discounts, and family-building benefits. In the U.S., we cover 100% of premiums for employees. International benefits align with local standards.
  • Time Off to Recharge: Paid time off so you can truly unplug. U.S.: 15 PTO days (increasing to 20 after 2 years) + 8 paid holidays. International policies vary by country.
  • Financial Peace of Mind: Company-paid life, short-term, and long-term disability insurance where available.
  • Performance-Driven Culture: Join a fast-moving, ambitious, and collaborative team that wins together.
  • Referral Rewards: Earn bonuses for bringing top talent to the team.
  • Planning for the Future: Long-term financial planning support. U.S.: 401(k) plan. International: region-specific savings programs where applicable.
  • Top-Tier Tech: Choose a Mac or PC, plus monitor, keyboard, and mouse to hit the ground running.

CharterUP is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive, accessible, and respectful workplace. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, ancestry, disability, medical condition, marital status, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws in the United States and Canada. If you require accommodation during the recruitment process, please let us know. CharterUP is committed to providing reasonable accommodations during the hiring process. If you need assistance or an accommodation, please contact your recruiter.

Hiring Locations: CharterUP U.S.-based candidates and employees must reside in one of the following states: Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Mississippi, Missouri, North Carolina, New Hampshire, Nevada, New York, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming.

We hire in the U.S. and Canada and are actively expanding our global footprint.

About the Role

As a Strategic Sourcer, you’ll be part of a new global sourcing hub focused on finding the right contributors for complex AI projects that require specialized or hard-to-reach talent across a wide range of domains, from translation and localization to legal, medical, scientific, and technical fields.

This is a strategic, hands-on role within Fulfillment. You will partner closely with the Sourcing Lead, Recruitment, and Delivery to turn complex requirements into effective searches, find creative ways to reach the right contributors, and rapidly scale sourcing efforts when projects require high volumes. The team will work in a data-informed and AI-enabled environment, using technology to enhance human judgment, creativity, and connection.

Your Impact

  • Design and execute creative sourcing strategies for specialized, hard-to-reach, and high-volume needs.
  • Explore communities, networks, referrals, and non-traditional channels to find and engage contributors.
  • Translate project requirements into targeted searches and adapt strategies as needs evolve.
  • Communicate sourcing progress, challenges, and market feedback, and flag potential risks.
  • Use sourcing and conversion data to identify bottlenecks, test approaches, and improve performance.
  • Use AI and automation in research, outreach, analysis, and sourcing workflows to improve efficiency.

What You Bring

  • 3+ years of experience in sourcing, recruitment, talent acquisition, or a related field.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
  • Strong research and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop new approaches when traditional sourcing methods are not effective.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • Experience using sourcing data and funnel metrics to inform decisions and improve results.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience sourcing for AI, data, or crowdsourcing projects.
  • Experience sourcing linguists, translators, or other language profiles across markets.
  • Experience working with global or distributed teams across time zones.
  • Flexibility to work regular U.S. hours or provide U.S. overlap when working in a different time zone.

Why You'll Love Working Here

At Appen, we foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and excellence. We value curiosity, accountability, and a commitment to delivering the highest quality AI solutions for frontier models.

You'll work on complex challenges that shape the future of AI across industries and geographies, alongside talented people in a culture that values humility over ego. You'll have the flexibility to deliver in a way that works for you and your team, supported by tools, resources, and development opportunities to continue to build your capability over time.

About Appen

Appen has been a leader in AI training data for over 30 years. We specialise in human generated data to train, fine tune, and evaluate models across generative AI, large language models, computer vision, and speech recognition. Our AI assisted data annotation platform and global crowd of more than 1 million contributors in over 200 countries support model pre training, supervised fine tuning, evaluation and benchmarking, safety and red teaming, and multilingual global expansion.

Endeavour has an exciting opportunity for someone passionate about sustainability and eager to be part of an innovative company that’s on a journey to transform the world’s infrastructure. We are seeking an IT Infrastructure & Operations Manager working directly with Endeavour’s IT team and focusing on technical issues, providing solutions, enhancing existing technology stack and implementing new infrastructure into our ecosystem. This role is part of the support team that services the entire our Endeavour ecosystem and contributes to the overall health and success of the organization.

The IT Infrastructure & Operations Manager needs to be agile, professional, and comfortable in a rapidly changing environment. The right person is trustworthy with confidential information, highly organized, self-motivated, has excellent communication skills, can think strategically, and works equally as well independently as with a team.

Endeavour is highly selective about the people we bring on board because our ecosystem depends on it. Change happens quickly here, and we must maintain a strong team of honest, communicative, collaborative, open-minded, strategic, reliable, and driven team members. We seek ultra-creatives and superstar performers with self-awareness, a sense of humility, and a hunger to make a positive impact in the world. Endeavour offers flexibility and endless growth opportunities to those who can harness their skills and talents and identify how and where to use them to add value. Our support team is the heart of the ecosystem. We’re a diverse group of bright, passionate, dedicated people, working together to make a real difference. Are you ready to join the journey?

Key Responsibilities

Include but are not limited to:

  • Manage the day-to-day operation, availability, and performance of the organization's IT infrastructure and operational services.
  • Lead and develop the IT Operations team, fostering a culture of accountability, customer service, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Administer and maintain enterprise infrastructure, including networking, servers, storage, cloud services, endpoint management, identity platforms, and collaboration technologies.
  • Oversee the administration, lifecycle management, and operational support of core SaaS platforms and IT systems, ensuring they remain secure, reliable, and aligned with business needs.
  • Plan and execute infrastructure upgrades, technology refreshes, and operational improvement initiatives to maintain a modern and resilient IT environment.
  • Manage enterprise backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity capabilities to minimize operational risk and downtime.

Education / Experience

  • Work in a fast-paced environment

A culture of respect, learning, and excellence.

raw.description:
Mission – Why we exist, what we do, and why we need you

SpotMe is a leading B2B event platform that helps enterprises increase the impact of their events by delivering CRM-connected, high-quality experiences across in-person, virtual, hybrid events, and webinars. With a strong focus on life sciences, SpotMe powers Onomi: an HCP engagement product that enables medical and commercial teams to run impactful congresses, symposia, advisory boards, and webinars. Together, SpotMe and Onomi turn events into a company’s most effective engagement channel.

This position is the ideal role for experienced talents in tech/services sales. With a self-driven resilient mindset, positive energy, and strong business acumen, you'll thrive in a fast paced environment. You will negotiate multi-year enterprise contracts, drive revenue and usage growth across our largest Fortune 500 accounts, and shape the long-term success of our most valued partnerships. Our top-performing Account Directors typically progress to sales leadership roles.

The Account Director role is key in our sales team and reports directly to the VP of Account Management. Following our Onomi launch, life sciences expansion pipeline is the #1 company objective, and driving revenue growth within existing customers is a key component.

As the account leader, you will be the primary point of contact for 7-15 key accounts with a total revenue of ~$3M and:

  • [40%] Identify and close expansion, upgrade and renewal opportunities.
  • [20%] Account retention and expansion plan execution: inserting Onomi into centers of excellence and delivery units, designing operating procedures for flawless execution, coordinating implementation and key integrations, evangelizing buying centers, functions and geo/affiliates with workshops and webinars, and partner engagement, briefing and certification.
  • [15%] Build relationships with key account stakeholders: engaging with new users, fostering trust-based relationships with champions and above-event stakeholders (commercial excellence, medical, IT, procurement), establishing open lines of communication with economic buyers, influencing HQ-prescribed technology usage guidelines, facilitating introductions and exec touchpoints at director/VP level with a meaningful briefing, demonstrating value in absolute ROI terms, and securing customer presence at customer advisory boards and 3rd-party events and roundtables.
  • [10%] Perform account research, mapping and planning: capturing intelligence on organization design, strategic priorities, Onomi's share of wallet, other vendors' scope, and integration, usage and investments for each use case; understanding budget cycles; partner mapping; and creating pricing benchmarks against other solutions.
  • [10%] Handle first-line account compliance, administrative and product inquiries.
  • [5%] Report on sales activities: CRM updates, sales forecasts and pipeline calls.

Objectives - The problems you will solve

In your first 1 month, you will:

  • Join our leadership team at live industry events: staff the booth at tradeshows and walk congresses with them
  • Master our core sales plays: rehearse them, listen to past winning calls, and successfully conduct an expansion mock demo call that convinces the team you can do it alone
  • Master our sales processes and systems (Salesforce, Google Suite, PowerPoint, Fathom) to be able to manage a sales lifecycle from customer request to contract expansion deals autonomously
  • Get introduced to all customers in your portfolio and secure face time with 80% of them.

In your first 3 months, you will:

  • Close your first deal autonomously
  • Identify 2 expansion levers for each account, with goals and steps documented in Salesforce
  • Attend your first congress solo, with a pre-event target list, a floor contact log, and 100% follow-up
  • Complete your account research and planning for every account in your portfolio, including renewal strategy and budget insertion

After the first 6 months, key indicators (usage and logo revenue) are trending up

After 12 months, you will:

  • Have met 100% of your customer portfolio in person at least once and met 1-3 new influential stakeholders per account
  • Have executed your account plans and achieved an aggregate 20% YoY revenue growth on your portfolio through services and/or software expansion

What you need to be great at:

  • Account leadership: You are above all a true account leader in B2B SaaS or services/consulting - you have managed large accounts ($200K-$2M) in large companies (>500 employees) over time, and you are able to truly understand the decision-making process and buying centers, and establish and nurture relationships with key people to expand scope and volume. You know what it means to operate a global, large-scale account in a first-class fashion.
  • Industry expertise with business orientation: You bring experience selling into or leading accounts in critical industries (pharma, financial services, professional services, or tech), whether at a SaaS company, an agency, or a consultancy, with a track record of working with the most demanding customers. Above all, you have a flair for spotting pain points, helping customers form business cases, and guiding them toward execution. Pharma HCP engagement expertise, with all its nuances (medical, commercial, marketing), is a plus but not a must.
  • Autonomy and resourcefulness: You create your own pipeline rather than waiting for deals to arrive, and you'll happily staff a congress booth solo for three days to do it. You make decisions with confidence and don't wait to be told what to do. When you hit a wall, you find a way around it. You're scrappy, creative, and solution-oriented by nature, and you act proactively even when there's no immediate commercial upside.
  • Commercial sharpness: You run numbers quickly, think several steps ahead in negotiations, and understand what truly drives your customers' business. You can build a solid business case that holds up in front of a C-suite or procurement team, and you are comfortable making decisions and forming working hypotheses even when you don't have all the facts.
  • Customer and product depth: You want to understand why a customer's organization works the way it does: how decisions get made, where the friction sits, and what sits beneath the stated need. You know the product well enough to handle the hard questions yourself and shape a solution in the room, bringing in specialists when they add something you can't, not as a substitute for knowing the answer.
  • Coachability at speed: We invest heavily in coaching, and we look for people who welcome it at any stage of their career. You take direct feedback without defensiveness, and what we sharpen with you one day shows up in your next customer conversation.

SpotMe recruits, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, parental status, or veteran status.

raw.title: Staff Software Engineer
raw.excerpt: Beacon Biosignals is transforming precision medicine for the brain, from clinical development to clinical care.
raw.description:
Beacon Biosignals is transforming precision medicine for the brain, from clinical development to clinical care. For Life Sciences partners, we offer the leading at-home EEG platform for clinical development of novel therapeutics for neurological, psychiatric, and sleep disorders. Our Diagnostics business is building the most comprehensive at-home platform for precision diagnostics, combining EEG and cardiopulmonary signals to deliver reimbursable assessments for sleep and central nervous system disorders. Together, we're changing the way patients are diagnosed and treated for any disorder that affects brain physiology.

Beacon Biosignals is seeking a Staff Software Engineer to join our Datastore team. The Datastore sits at the heart of Beacon's platform. It defines our foundational data model and serves as the centralized repository and API for brain data collected from clinical studies, supporting the analytical tools, services, and applications used by our scientists, clinicians, and partners.

This role emphasizes the design and scaling of backend systems for data infrastructure: PostgreSQL data models, Kafka-driven event pipelines, and the GraphQL API that makes scientific and clinical data usable - distinct from frontend development or end-user product surfaces. At this level you will lead the design of complex systems within the Datastore rather than individual components, own the pipelines that deliver dataset snapshots into our warehouse, and collaborate across platform, application and scientific teams to implement APIs that unlock new workflows in Beacon's expanding portfolio of clinical studies and digital health products.

You should have experience writing complex SQL queries by hand, and should be prepared to reason about schema design, indexes, and query behavior as a matter of course.

Two properties of our system that shape our work may influence your application. Our GraphQL API is generated from the PostgreSQL schema using PostGraphile, so a schema decision is an API decision. Secondly, row-level security is in force on effectively every table, because clinical data from different studies and partners shares one schema, with some rows shared for access by multiple internal teams. RLS predicates get injected into your queries, which makes reasoning about query plans genuinely harder here than it is in most places. If that sounds interesting rather than tedious, you'll enjoy this team.

We are hiring two engineers into this role, with two different centers of gravity. One will focus on the breadth of the Datastore: the event pipelines, the GraphQL API, core data models, and third-party integrations. The other will focus on depth in PostgreSQL (data modeling, performance tuning, operations) and supporting all engineers in developing schemas and the access controls that protect clinical data. The core requirements are the same. Tell us which one you are most drawn to in your application.

This role is 100% remote from anywhere in the U.S. Beacon's robust asynchronous work practices ensure a first-class remote work experience, but we also have in-person office hubs in Boston, New York City, and Paris.

What success looks like

  • You lead design and architecture for complex projects and systems within the Datastore, weighing implementation trade-offs with engineering principles and backing your decisions with data rather than preference
  • You partner with product managers, scientific and clinical stakeholders, and other development and support teams to translate their requirements into new integrations, services, and solutions for scaling Beacon's data platform - contributing to broader product and technical decisions, not simply implementing them
  • You debug and profile ambiguous problems that cross system boundaries, including codebases beyond the Datastore's purview, and you leave what you touch better than you found it — structure, test coverage, tooling
  • Peers look to your work as an example: you implement features with attention to detail, demonstrating product awareness and high standards for data integrity, design soundness, and maintainability across the lifespan of the system
  • You draft RFCs to lead complex feature discovery and technical design phases, soliciting and incorporating input, and helping your team align on a set of decisions to guide development
  • You plan your own work and contribute to planning the team's, making reasoned trade-offs between speed, generalizability, and technical debt, and accounting for the needs of multiple stakeholder teams
  • You teach and mentor other engineers regularly, give feedback that people act on, and are sought out for it. You may act as tech lead on a project or as the coordination point for engineering practice within the team
  • You leverage feedback from internal stakeholders and external partners to improve operational robustness and ease of use of the Datastore and its services via new documentation, tools, and dashboards

What you will bring

  • 7+ years of backend development experience, including at least 3 years focused on data platforms and backend infrastructure for data-centric applications: transactional systems, event pipelines, and the APIs that serve them
  • Highly proficient in at least one technical area relevant to this work: data modeling, distributed systems, API design, or database engineering, with the depth that others on a team come to you for
  • Strong proficiency in SQL, with production experience working with PostgreSQL as an application database; you write and tune queries fluently and are comfortable reasoning about schema design, indexes, and query plans
  • Hands-on experience with data streaming and event processing, using Kafka (our event bus) or an equivalent such as RabbitMQ, Pulsar, or a cloud-based equivalent like Amazon Kinesis
  • Proficiency in Julia or Python; Julia is a core Datastore language, and experience with Julia is a strong plus, but not required — we welcome candidates eager to learn it!
  • Experience deploying and operating services in containerized environments, with familiarity in Kubernetes and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools such as Terraform and/or Helm
  • A track record of mentoring engineers and improving how a team works - practices, tooling, test coverage, or documentation that outlasted your involvement
  • A collaborative mindset: you enjoy working across disciplines and believe people achieve more together than alone
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, especially in asynchronous and remote-friendly environments
  • A self-directed approach, with a track record of thriving in hybrid or fully remote teams
  • Experience with, or interest in, using LLM-assisted or agentic coding tools in a production setting, with good judgment about what guardrails are needed

For the Datastore Systems role:

  • You can lead design across the breadth of the platform.
  • GraphQL and TypeScript/JavaScript (Node.js) - GraphQL is the Datastore's primary interface, and this profile owns significant parts of it
  • Designing event-driven pipelines end to end: producers, consumers, replay, idempotency, and what happens when a consumer falls behind
  • Leading the design of complex systems rather than individual components, across the API, the pipelines, and the services that depend on them

For the PostgreSQL & Data Modeling role:

  • You can be the person the rest of the team comes to about the database.
  • Deep PostgreSQL: you reason fluently about the query planner, index selection, and EXPLAIN (ANALYZE), and why a query that should be fast isn't
  • Data modeling: you design the schema itself: entities, relationships, and the constraints that make invalid states impossible. Including how to model time, since clinical results get re-scored and corrected and we need to answer "what did this look like when the report was signed?"
  • Schema evolution under load: zero-downtime migrations, dual-write transitions, lock avoidance, backfill and verification. Our schema has hundreds of migrations behind it and will have hundreds more
  • Operating PostgreSQL in production, not only designing for it: upgrades, replication, backup and restore, connection pooling, bloat and vacuum behaviour, extensions
  • Making others good at it: you teach, review, and document, because a schema only stays coherent if the team understands it

We don't expect every candidate to check every box. If you bring strong fundamentals, care about data infrastructure for health, and are excited to learn, we’d love to hear from you!

The US-based salary range for this role is $170,000 – $190,000. Salary ranges are determined using current market compensation data for this role and adjusted based on experience, skills, and location. The base salary is one component of the total compensation package, which includes equity, PTO and other benefits.

At Beacon, we've found that cultural and scientific impact is driven most by those that lead by example. As such, we're always seeking new contributors whose work demonstrates an avid curiosity, a bias towards simplicity, an eye for composability, a self-service mindset, and - most of all - a deep empathy towards colleagues, stakeholders, users, and patients. We believe a diverse team builds more robust systems and achieves higher impact.

As part of Zillow Group’s FinTech division, you’ll help reshape how consumers buy, sell, and finance homes while working in a collaborative, high-energy environment. We’re a team of innovators, problem solvers, and creative individuals pushing the boundaries of the mortgage industry.

Mortgage Loan Officers at Zillow Home Loans, drive their success through one of two specialized lending teams.

One team leverages a high volume, lead driven, phone-based environment for Loan Officers who excel at high-frequency conversion and scaling customer relationships quickly.

The other team focuses on a consultative, market-based model for those who thrive on building long-term strategic partnerships with Zillow Preferred Agents.

Both teams are core to our purchase-focused mission and are equally backed by Zillow’s industry-leading technology, brand, centralized operations, and leadership support. Whether you find your edge in data-driven, lead-responsive execution or in nurturing a local professional network, both paths offer a high-impact career within the Zillow ecosystem.

You’ll guide borrowers from first contact through funding while delivering a best-in-class customer experience. Based on your background and strengths, you may operate in either a high-volume, digitally driven environment or a relationship-based, market-focused model. Success in this role comes from responsiveness, execution, and performance in a structured, metrics-driven organization—supported by Zillow’s brand, platform, and operational scale.

This role is “remote” with restrictions. Your designated remote location is defined as your principal place of residence, which must be physically located within the state listed above Mississippi. Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location. Employees in this role will not be paid below the salary threshold for exempt employees in the state where they reside.

The role is focused on measurement, specification accuracy and quantities. Supplier pricing and purchasing decisions remain with the Business Owner initially.

  • Review drawings and project documentation

  • Complete accurate fencing and gate take-offs
    Measure fence lengths by type/location, identify height changes, corners, slopes and stepped sections, separate gate openings and calculate the required components for each system.
  • Prepare complete material and component breakdowns
    Quantify posts, panels, rails, palings, sheets, slats, mesh, wire, brackets, caps, fixings, gate frames, hardware, automation components, concrete/footings and other required accessories.
  • Produce itemised Bills of Materials
    Create Excel schedules grouped by fence type, gate, location or supplier category, clearly recording drawing references, descriptions, dimensions, specifications, units, net quantities, allowances and total required quantities.
  • Maintain accuracy, traceability and revision control
    Provide marked-up drawings supporting each schedule, identify unresolved items, maintain a query register, update quantities when drawings change and ensure schedules remain traceable to the correct revision.

Requirements

SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience and competency reading construction and shop drawings.

  • Understanding how individual components form a complete construction/fabrication system.

  • Managing several take-offs and identifying missing or inconsistent information.

  • Clear written and spoken English.

  • Able to raise queries promptly.

  • Able to communicate with the Business Owner, Project Manager, factory and installation teams.

  • Comfortable seeking clarification rather than making assumptions where information is incomplete.

Executive Director, California College Guidance Initiative

100% Remote within California; must reside in California


The Foundation for California Community Colleges (FoundationCCC) is the official nonprofit auxiliary to the California Community Colleges, the largest and most diverse system of higher education in the nation. Founded in 1998, FoundationCCC has served as a catalyst for student success, workforce development, and community impact across California. The organization manages over 70 programs and initiatives that expand opportunity and accelerate pathways to economic and social mobility for all Californians — piloting new approaches, replicating promising practices, and scaling sustainable methods to support all 116 California community colleges and 2.2 million students.


Since its founding, FoundationCCC has delivered hundreds of millions in grants, support, and cost savings to colleges, and 86% of every dollar that comes into FoundationCCC directly supports programs and services that benefit the colleges and their students. FoundationCCC plays a pivotal role in forging new partnerships and accelerating bold approaches to advance the California Community Colleges and the communities they serve.


About CCGI

The California College Guidance Initiative (CCGI) manages CaliforniaColleges.edu, the state's official college and career planning platform. CCGI is a legislatively authorized service provider to all California school districts as established in California Education Code Section 60900.5. CaliforniaColleges.edu helps students explore college and career options, launch their college and financial aid applications, and access financial aid lessons, all on one site. It helps educators utilize data-driven guidance and streamline student support, while allowing parents and guardians to view and monitor their student's progress. By connecting information, planning, and application processes, CCGI strengthens college and career readiness and expands access to postsecondary opportunities statewide.


CCGI partners with K-12 school districts across the state to give students, families, and counselors the tools they need to ensure that all California students, especially those who have been underrepresented in higher education, can move seamlessly from K-12 to college and career. The organization serves more than 650 local educational agencies, transmitting transcript data, powering transcript-informed tools, and streamlining applications for college admissions and financial aid.


CCGI operates as a structurally embedded project under the fiscal sponsorship of FoundationCCC and is a Collaborative Impact Partner of the organization. This partnership allows CCGI to focus entirely on its data-driven mission to support California students while leveraging the robust administrative infrastructure of the community college system's official nonprofit partner. The fiscal partnership model reflects how FoundationCCC works across California's education landscape: incubating and scaling high-impact initiatives that strengthen the pipeline from K-12 into the California community colleges and beyond.

The organization employs roughly 80 staff distributed across four divisions: Programs, CaliforniaColleges.edu, Data and Strategy, and Operations, with regional teams spanning the state.


The Role

CCGI's next Executive Director will guide the organization's strategic direction, strengthen its statewide relationships, and oversee a leadership team accountable for delivering its mission and statutory responsibilities. This leader will connect education policy, partnerships, organizational resources, and execution to reduce barriers and expand students' access to college and career pathways. The role reports to FoundationCCC as the most senior CCGI leader and serves as CCGI's most critical and influential advocate with leadership at the state's public educational institutions, the state legislature, the Governor's office, and the Department of Finance.


What We Are Seeking


Strategic Direction and Execution

Sets clear priorities, articulates a compelling future for CCGI — expanding into areas like deepening platform adoption and leveraging data more powerfully — while simultaneously managing the practical realities of funding constraints, statutory compliance, and intersegmental coordination. Translates strategy into measurable outcomes and resource decisions and adjusts direction as student needs and statewide conditions evolve.


Statewide Relationship-Based Leadership

Builds and deepens trust across education systems and government partners — including 650+ K-12 Local Education Agencies, the California Department of Education, the California Community Colleges, California State University, the University of California, the California Student Aid Commission and the Cradle-to-Career Data System. Navigates competing priorities with diplomacy and develops coalitions that advance shared outcomes through influence rather than positional authority.


Team-Centered Stewardship

Honors the deep expertise of the existing team, provides clarity and resources so divisions can execute, builds strong retention, and enters the organization with humility. Leads through senior leaders, clarifies decision-making authority, strengthens accountability, and develops leadership capacity across the organization.


Financial and Organizational Stewardship

Accountable for both long-term financial sustainability through continued state funding, philanthropy funding opportunities, and cybersecurity and risk management


Student-Centered, Equity-Informed Judgment

Uses evidence and stakeholder perspectives to identify barriers and make decisions that improve educational access and opportunity — especially for students most harmed by misalignment between education systems.


Communication and Culture

Communicates clearly across audiences, welcomes constructive disagreement, provides direct and respectful feedback, and models collaboration, learning, and accountability.


Essential Responsibilities

MISSION AND STRATEGIC ALIGNMENT

  • Provides executive leadership to position CCGI to effectively achieve its mission, statutory responsibilities, and long-term strategic objectives.
  • Establishes CCGI's medium- and long-term strategic direction in alignment with its mission, statutory responsibilities, FoundationCCC's mission, and evolving statewide education priorities.
  • Translates strategic direction into clear annual and multi-year priorities, outcomes, and resource commitments.
  • Holds executive leaders accountable for organizational performance and uses data, results, and changing conditions to assess progress and adjust strategy.
  • Anticipates changes in the external environment and positions CCGI to respond effectively to emerging policy, funding, technology, and educational priorities.
  • Champions innovative, scalable solutions that reduce systemic barriers, lessen administrative burden, and improve student access to college and career pathways.

ORGANIZATIONAL STEWARDSHIP

  • Provides overall executive leadership, direction, and accountability for CCGI's strategy, operations, organizational performance, and impact.
  • Leads and supports CCGI's leadership team, providing direction and counsel to division leaders on strategic, financial, operational, and organizational decisions.
  • Establishes clear decision-making authority, accountability, and expectations across the executive team and organization.
  • Builds and develops a cohesive, high-performing leadership team capable of advancing shared priorities.
  • Ensures organizational structures, leadership capacity, systems, and resources support effective execution of CCGI's mission and strategy while maintaining alignment with FoundationCCC's mission.
  • Maintains an organizational culture grounded in CCGI's mission and values, reinforcing collaboration, accountability, innovation, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
  • Proactively oversees legal, financial, operational, cybersecurity, compliance, and reputational risk and ensures appropriate controls and practices are in place.

EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT

  • Serves as a principal executive representative for CCGI with education leaders, state officials, policymakers, partners, funders, and other key stakeholders.
  • Cultivates and sustains long-term strategic relationships with leaders and organizations across education segments, state agencies, governmental entities, and other key partners.
  • Builds and sustains strategic coalitions that strengthen alignment across education systems and advance CCGI's mission and statewide impact.
  • Exercises diplomacy, political acumen, and executive communication to navigate complex stakeholder environments and strengthen CCGI's visibility, credibility, and influence.
  • Leads the annual and multi-year budgeting process in coordination with the Department of Finance, Legislature, and other appropriate stakeholders.
  • Ensures CCGI fulfills its statutory purpose and responsibilities as established in California law and applicable state requirements.
  • Maintains executive accountability for legislative reporting, funding requirements, governmental commitments, and other state oversight obligations.
  • Ensures the Cradle-to-Career Data System Governing Board and other appropriate state constituents are informed of CCGI's work, priorities, progress, and significant organizational developments.

Experience and Knowledge

  • Organizational leadership — Experience leading a distributed team of 50+ through an executive leadership structure.  
  • Equity-centered strategy — Demonstrated ability to translate equity commitments into organizational policy, hiring, and partnerships. 
  • Government relations — Experience working with or within the Legislature, Governor's office, or Department of Finance on education policy or funding. 
  • California education ecosystem — Deep familiarity with K-12, community colleges, CSU, UC, and the state agencies that connect them. 
  • Government relations — Experience working with or within the Legislature, Governor's office, or Department of Finance on education policy or funding. 
  • Intersegmental/Cross-Sector coordination — Track record of building alignment across institutional boundaries with competing priorities. 
  • Organizational leadership — Experience leading a distributed team of 50+ through an executive leadership structure. 
  • Data-informed operations — Comfort with data systems, student data privacy and related legal requirements, and using evidence to drive strategy. 
  • Financial stewardship — Budgeting, forecasting, resource allocation, and managing state funding relationships. 
  • Equity-centered strategy — Demonstrated ability to translate equity commitments into organizational policy, hiring, and partnerships. 
  • Nonprofit and public-sector context — Understanding regulatory compliance, contracting, and the constraints of operating as a public-facing nonprofit. 

Leadership Qualities

  • Integrity and trustworthiness — Authentic, transparent, and consistent in word and action.
  • Relationship-first approach — Builds coalition through genuine engagement, not positional authority.
  • Humility and curiosity — Enters with respect for what the team has built; listens before acting.
  • Political sophistication — Comfortable in ambiguity; reads institutional dynamics and acts accordingly.
  • Courageous advocacy — Willing to champion CCGI's mission and its team in high-stakes settings.
  • Communication clarity — Can articulate complex intersegmental work to legislators, educators, and students alike.
  • Vulnerability and self-reflection — Models the feedback culture CCGI values, including Nonviolent Communication.
  • Long-term commitment — Sees this as a calling, not a stepping stone.

Cultural Alignment

CCGI's team culture is built on nine characteristics that are deeply embedded in how the organization works. The next leader must not only endorse these qualities but model them daily:

Collaboration and learning · Data-driven practices · Direct feedback

Documentation · Due diligence and preparation · Professionalism and kindness

Self-reflection · Strategic thinking · Vulnerability

The Executive Director sets the tone for this culture and is expected to model, provide, and receive feedback using the Nonviolent Communication framework.

What we Offer

FoundationCCC is fully committed to a “remote-first” philosophy, and recruits and hires talent across the state in fully remote positions, where virtual work is possible. Our headquarters are located in Downtown Sacramento, just blocks from California’s State Capitol.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation, generous PTO, and paid holidays
  • Medical, dental, and vision plans, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts (HSA), Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and Wellness offerings
  • CalPERS retirement program and optional 403(b) and 457 Retirement plans
  • Carrot reproductive health and fertility support
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Public Service Loan Forgiveness certified employer

Working Hours, Location, and Travel 

Hours: Full-time position, 40 hours per week, with additional hours needed to address the organization’s needs.

Location: California-based with the flexibility to work remotely (in California). 

Travel: Regular daytime travel and in-person attendance at events and meetings within the state to align with the needs of the institutions in the state. Overnight travel (up to 20%) by land and air.

raw.excerpt: At Signifyd, we help merchants confidently grow their businesses by building trusted relationships with their customers.
raw.description:
At Signifyd, we help merchants confidently grow their businesses by building trusted relationships with their customers. Our advanced technology, combined with a team genuinely invested in our clients’ success, creates frictionless shopping experiences, approving more good orders, protecting revenue, and keeping customers happy.

Trusted by thousands of leading merchants across more than 100 countries, we securely process billions of transactions each year. Our people are the heart of everything we do, driving our mission forward with commitment, empathy, and creativity. Join us on our mission to empower confident, fraud-free commerce by helping online retailers provide superior customer experiences and eliminate fraud. Learn about our company values here!

Department: Engineering

The Engineering organization at Signifyd is at the forefront of building solutions that protect and empower global commerce. We pride ourselves on delivering highly scalable, robust systems that evolve with our customers' needs, from emerging startups to enterprise-level organizations processing millions of transactions. Our engineers thrive in an innovative environment where rapid iteration and continuous learning drive our success. We embrace modern development practices, leverage cloud-native technologies, and maintain a customer-obsessed mindset to ensure our solutions anticipate tomorrow's challenges. Strong partnerships with Product and Data Science ensure every technical decision is aligned with delivering maximum value and driving meaningful business outcomes.

The Role

We are looking for a staff back-end engineer to set the technical direction for the platform retailers use to integrate with Signifyd. As a member of the Integrations & Onboarding team, you will own the architecture and long-term health of our public-facing API platform and ingestion services, defining both what we build and how we build it. This role suits an engineer who is drawn to open-ended problems spanning several teams, who can turn a complicated problem space into simple and durable foundations, and whose influence shows up in other teams' roadmaps as much as in their own systems.

Responsibilities

  • Define and deliver the multi-year technical vision for our integration and ingestion platform across multiple teams and competing constraints.
  • Make the architecture-level technology calls, including build-versus-buy decisions and framework selection, and own the tradeoffs behind them.
  • Own the overall health and engineering quality of the platform: drive health reviews, curate testing strategy, and ensure the systems stay maintainable by engineers with varying levels of expertise.
  • Design systems under significant ambiguity, particularly those that many other systems depend on.
  • Partner with product management, data engineering, and other engineering teams, influencing their roadmaps where a shared solution serves the business better than a locally optimal one.
  • Raise the technical bar across related areas through design and code review, with particular attention to cross-team interfaces and API quality.
  • Proactively identify areas of technical debt and drive the strategy for addressing them.
  • Serve as a role model and mentor for engineers across the organization, and champion responsible adoption of AI development tools.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • Significant experience in software development with modern programming languages, experience programming in a functional style.
  • Track record of setting technical direction across multiple teams, and of carrying large, ambiguous initiatives through to completion.
  • Depth in a platform or product domain that translated into distinctive business value, rather than breadth alone.
  • Strong software design and architecture skills, including reducing complex problems to simple foundational components and designing interfaces that are difficult to misuse.
  • Experience owning the long-term health of a significant system: testing strategy, operability, and reducing key-person dependency.
  • Experience building distributed systems or public-facing/platform APIs at scale.
  • Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP.
  • Ability to influence without authority, and to communicate effectively with engineers and non-engineers alike.
  • You use modern AI development tools fluently and help others do the same, championing responsible adoption while holding the line on quality. This means practical experience with AI coding assistants, understanding how to provide effective context, critically evaluating generated code for correctness, security, and maintainability, and coaching others toward the same standard.

Our Stack

  • Java, SQL, gRPC, HTTP/REST
  • Kubernetes, Docker, Linux
  • Cassandra, Pub/Sub, Bigtable, Databricks
  • GCP, AWS

Benefits in our US offices:

  • Discretionary Time Off Policy (Unlimited!)
  • 401K Match
  • Stock Options
  • Annual Performance Bonus or Commissions
  • Paid Parental Leave (12 weeks)
  • On-Demand Therapy for all employees & their dependents
  • Dedicated learning budget through Learnerbly
  • Health Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
  • Short Term and Long Term Disability Insurance
  • Life Insurance
  • Company Social Events
  • Signifyd Swag

Compensation:

In the United States, each work location is assigned a specific pay zone, which determines the salary range for a given position. The starting base salary for the selected candidate will be based on a variety of factors, including job-related skills, experience, qualifications, geographic location, and current market conditions.

Base Salary Ranges by Pay Zone:

  • Tier 1 (NYC/SF Bay Area/Seattle): $200,000 - 225,000 annually
    Tier 2 (DC Metro/Austin/Chicago/Denver/Boston/Los Angeles/San Diego): $195,000- $220,000 annually
    Tier 3 (US - All Other): $190,000- $215,000 annually

Equity: This role is eligible for a stock option grant of 6000 stock options, based on the position level and internal compensation guidelines.

Bonus: This role is eligible for an annual performance bonus of up to 10% of base salary.

We want to provide an inclusive interview experience for all, including people with disabilities. We are happy to provide reasonable accommodations to candidates in need of individualized support during the hiring process.

Location: within European time zones.

About Pet Media Group

Pet Media Group (PMG) acquires, launches and develops leading pet and equestrian marketplaces around the world. We operate eight brands across seven markets in the UK, US, Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands, Italy and Spain. Every year, 1.7 million pets and horses find a new home through our platforms, and our flagship platforms include Pets4Homes.co.uk, Deine-Tierwelt.de and Lancasterpuppies.com.

The pet rehoming experience has remained largely unchanged for decades. At PMG, we're on a mission to transform it by making it more trusted, safe and convenient through technology. We're a driven, ambitious team with a track record of building unicorns, backed by investors such as Verdane. We've been profitable since our first year, so we don't rely on investor capital to grow.

The opportunity

CLM is changing, and we want to rethink what it looks like when AI, automation and customer data sit at the heart of how we work. Our CRM covers email, push, in app and SMS for buyers and breeders across our marketplaces, with more markets joining as the group grows.

As our CRM & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own key parts of the customer lifecycle with our Head of CLM, across strategy, data, automation and execution. You'll spot where engagement can improve, design new journeys and experiments, and build the workflows that bring them to life.

You'll also help shape how the CLM itself works. Successful experiments become repeatable systems, and work that doesn't need a person gets automated.

Your edge is building fast and measuring everything. You use AI daily for research, analysis, segmentation, copy, personalisation and testing, so running several markets does not mean several times the work.

What you will do

  • Own the customer lifecycle. Design journeys for buyers and breeders that respond to what they do, across email, push, in app and SMS.

  • Turn data into action. Dig into behavioural data, spot opportunities and turn them into relevant experiences.

  • Automate the repetitive. Turn manual CRM processes into automated workflows, so time goes to higher value work.

  • Test what AI makes possible. Experiment with personalisation, content and segmentation, measure the results and take what works into production.

  • Build for scale. Create reusable journeys and processes, ready for new markets as the group grows.

  • Work across the business. Partner with product, data, engineering and marketing on the customer experience and the infrastructure behind it.

Requirements

Must have experience

  • 4 or more years in CRM or lifecycle marketing, preferably in house, with campaigns you personally built that moved a metric you can name. Marketplace, consumer app or ecommerce experience is a strong plus.

  • Hands on experience in Customer.io or a comparable platform such as Braze, Iterable or Klaviyo. You're comfortable with segmentation logic, events, attributes and journeys that branch.

  • A habit of measuring. You set up tests properly, read results critically and sanity check a number before anyone else does.

  • Daily, active use of AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT for building, copy, QA, localisation and workflow automation. You have a clear view of what to automate and what stays human.

  • Fluent English, written to a standard that needs no editing before it reaches a customer.

  • Able to own CRM as a team of one when needed: briefing agencies and freelancers, holding them to account, and saying "not this week" to requests with a clear reason.

Preferable experience

  • HTML and Liquid for email templates.

  • SQL, or working with a data warehouse and product analytics.

  • Marketing automation beyond the CRM, such as webhooks or tools like n8n.

  • A CRM platform migration.

  • A two sided or reputation exposed marketplace, such as pets, dating, fintech or the gig economy.

You will thrive here if you

  • Have the mindset of a hands on builder rather than a delegator.

  • Believe process serves outcomes, not the other way around.

  • Value clarity, candour and collaboration.

  • Take a roadmap and run with it, without needing daily direction.

  • Are curious beyond CLM and happy to pick up other marketing projects.

  • Are excited by the challenge of scaling one of Europe's most impactful consumer marketplaces.

What we offer

  • Direct access to founders and country leads.

  • A profitable, growing business rather than a slide deck.

  • A diverse team of more than 100 colleagues across the world.

  • Competitive compensation.

raw.description:
Overview

Otter Products is looking for a Director of Retail Sales to lead our team. This role can be based remotely anywhere in the US.

The Director, Retail Sales leads a team of sales professionals responsible for the strategic direction, sales, and account management for the retail sales channel. This role will be responsible for developing strategic plans and resource allocation, using extensive knowledge of the business, sales techniques, and marketing strategies to attain overall revenue and profitability targets to achieve company objectives. Additionally, the Director, Retail Sales applies advanced leadership skills to support the professional growth of their direct reports and the broader sales team. This is a people leader role.

About Otter Products

At Otter Products, we protect what’s important. From our founder’s garage in 1998 to the global technology leader we are today, Otter Products continues to drive growth through innovation and sense of purpose. Through our industry-leading brands – OtterBox and OtterCares – we provide our partners and customers the number one selling and most trusted products in our categories. Our commitment to excellence and our philanthropic spirit is the foundation on which we foster our partner relationships, allowing us to grow and to give - together. By way of our charitable arm, the OtterCares Foundation, we support our communities and invest in the future through education that inspires kids to change the world. Our founder’s core values are still at the heart of everything we do. We measure our success not just by business results, but by our ability to give back to our communities and strengthen opportunities for all. To learn more, visit www.otterbox.com/pages/careers.

Responsibilities

  • Leadership and Development
    • Establish and provide resources to reach performance goals for all team members.
    • Team leadership responsibilities include talent development strategies and assessments, bi-weekly or monthly check-ins, career path support, succession planning and performance management/corrective action (when applicable).
    • Influence team to deliver unified business plan and overall working relationship.
    • Partner with Product and Merchandising team to provide feedback and guidance on new product opportunities.
  • Core Sales and Account Management
    • Full P&L accountability for retail sales channel.
    • Oversee current and new revenue streams, projects, and products to drive growth in sales.
    • Establish/strengthen/manage high level relationships within retail channel.
    • Collaborate with National Account Managers and other departments to streamline operations and manage inventory levels.
  • C-Level Engagement
    • Participate in strategic operations meetings and leadership team meetings to provide accurate sales and marketing data.
    • Partner with senior leaders to offer recommendations contributing to strategic initiatives.
  • Business Forecasting and Planning
    • Develop monthly, quarterly, and annual retail sales budgets, goals, and plans.
    • Analyze sales results and financial reports to make data-driven decisions, address performance gaps, and identify opportunities to drive continuous improvement.
    • Partner with Demand Planning to ensure plans are updated and meet all timelines.
  • Marketing and Merchandising
    • Collaborate with Channel Marketing to utilize Market Development Funds (MDF) budgets to drive retail sell through.
    • Manage MDF budget.
    • Collaborate with Brand Marketing team to establish channel expectations for brand marketing.
    • Coordinate business critical activities in conjunction with Merchandising and other stakeholders for all promotions and evaluate effectiveness adjusting strategies as needed.
  • Sales Training and Awareness
    • Develop monthly retail updates to provide organizational updates regarding retail wins.
    • Partner with product and merchandising teams to develop comprehensive sales training programs and implement ongoing team education.
  • Support and maintain a positive safety culture by following all safety policies and procedures and actively contributing to a safe working environment.
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree required. Experience in lieu of degree may be considered
  • Minimum of ten years of experience in managing national sales account activity is required.
  • Minimum of four years of experience in in a manager or higher-level role is required.
  • Experience working with national retailers, i.e., Target, Walmart, and BestBuy required.
  • Travel up to 50% required.

EEO

Otter Products, LLC is an equal employment opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic or status protected by law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act and in accordance with all other applicable federal, state and local laws.

USD $165,000.00/Yr.

USD $210,000.00/Yr.

Additional Total Rewards

Otter Products offers a robust benefits package to eligible employees including medical, dental, vision, basic life, voluntary life, long-term and short-term disability, employee assistance program, flexible spending accounts, health savings account, and 401(k) retirement plan. Additionally, for eligible employees, we offer accrued paid time off based on seniority, volunteer time off, parental leave, bereavement leave, company holidays, and years of service awards. raw.excerpt: About the roleAgile Six is looking for a senior market development leader to grow our work across the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), the broader U.
raw.description:
About the role

Agile Six is looking for a senior market development leader to grow our work across the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), the broader U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and the federal health information technology landscape.

We have more than a decade of delivery experience at CMS and HHS, including work in payment modernization, quality programs, agile transformation, and grants modernization. This role will build from that foundation, deepening our presence across CMS first, while identifying strategic opportunities across HHS and health IT where our experience and delivery model give us a meaningful advantage.

This is a highly autonomous role with significant responsibility for shaping where Agile Six invests, which opportunities we pursue, and how we develop relationships and partnerships in the market. As a self-managed organization, “Director” reflects the scope, accountability, and external leadership of the role rather than traditional people-management authority. Success is more than generating pipeline or revenue. We want to pursue work that aligns with our capabilities, values, and ability to deliver meaningful outcomes for government partners.

What you'll do

Develop and execute our CMS/HHS market strategy

  • Build and maintain a clear understanding of CMS centers and offices, decision-makers, modernization priorities, acquisition patterns, contract vehicles, incumbents, and upcoming opportunities.
  • Translate market intelligence into a prioritized strategy for where Agile Six should invest time, relationships, and pursuit resources.
  • Extend that strategy into adjacent HHS and health IT opportunities where our CMS experience creates a credible foundation.

Build relationships and shape opportunities

  • Develop trusted relationships with government leaders, industry partners, primes, and other stakeholders across CMS and HHS.
  • Represent Agile Six at relevant industry events, conferences, and partner conversations.
  • Identify opportunities early enough to help shape stronger solutions and acquisition approaches rather than simply responding to released solicitations.

Own and develop a qualified pipeline

  • Build and maintain a disciplined pipeline based on strategic fit, realistic win probability, delivery alignment, and potential impact.
  • Make thoughtful pursue/no-pursue recommendations and be willing to recommend walking away from work that is not right for Agile Six.
  • Connect pipeline planning with organizational forecasting and broader Market Development priorities.

Connect market development with delivery

  • Work closely with Agile Six delivery teams to understand our existing work, client needs, lessons learned, and potential areas for expansion.
  • Bring delivery expertise into opportunity shaping and ensure proposed work reflects what Agile Six can credibly and successfully deliver.
  • Help create relationships and opportunities that give future delivery teams a strong foundation for success.

Develop partnerships and solutions

  • Identify and develop teaming, subcontracting, and joint-venture opportunities that expand Agile Six's reach or capabilities.
  • Lead or support strategic partner and teaming negotiations while protecting the integrity of our delivery model.
  • Partner with Communications, Proposals, Delivery, Finance, Contracts, and company leadership throughout opportunity development and proposal work.

Strengthen how we do market development

  • Use AI-enabled tools to support research, market mapping, pipeline analysis, competitive intelligence, and opportunity development.
  • Contribute to shared Market Development practices, tools, intelligence, and strategy rather than operating as an individual sales function.
  • Help improve systems and practices that are still developing rather than waiting for perfect infrastructure.

What success looks like

In this role, you will:

  • Give Agile Six a substantially clearer view of the CMS market: where opportunities exist, where we have credibility, who we need to know, and where we should invest.
  • Build and deepen relationships across CMS centers and the broader HHS ecosystem that lead to qualified opportunities.
  • Develop a healthy pipeline of opportunities that balance growth potential with strategic and delivery fit.
  • Identify partnerships and teaming strategies that meaningfully expand Agile Six's ability to compete and deliver.
  • Help turn Agile Six's existing CMS/HHS delivery credibility into a larger, sustainable portfolio.
  • Strengthen the way Market Development and Delivery share intelligence and shape opportunities together.
  • Improve and make effective use of Agile Six's AI-enabled market development practices.

What we expect at this level

As a senior leader at Agile Six, you will be expected to:

  • Operate with significant autonomy and make sound decisions in areas where the path is not already defined.
  • Translate broad organizational goals into strategy, priorities, and measurable action.
  • Work effectively across organizational boundaries and influence outcomes without relying on positional authority.
  • Exercise judgment about where Agile Six should and should not invest.
  • Build alignment among people with different expertise, incentives, and perspectives.
  • Surface risks, gaps, and changing conditions early and recommend a path forward.
  • Strengthen organizational capability through what you build, learn, document, and share.
  • Represent Agile Six's values and interests thoughtfully in high-stakes external relationships.

What you'll bring

Required

  • Significant experience in business development, market development, partnerships, or a similar strategic role in federal technology, digital services, or consulting.
  • Deep familiarity with the CMS ecosystem, including how its centers operate, how technology services are procured, and the vehicles, partners, and incumbents that shape the market.
  • Working knowledge of the broader HHS landscape.
  • An established network within CMS and/or among organizations that work extensively with CMS.
  • Strong relationship-building and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to turn relationships and market knowledge into meaningful outcomes.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with delivery, contracts, finance, proposal, and/or other business functions.
  • Ability to evaluate opportunities strategically rather than simply maximize pipeline volume.
  • Experience using AI-enabled tools in your work, with sound judgment about where human expertise and context remain essential.
  • Comfort operating in a small, evolving organization where systems and processes may still be developing.

Helpful experience

  • Previous federal service at CMS or another HHS operating division.
  • Experience navigating CMS/HHS procurement and acquisition environments.
  • Familiarity with joint ventures, SDVOSB/8(a) partnerships, set-aside strategy, and federal teaming.
  • Experience with health IT domains such as quality measurement, payment modernization, interoperability, or grants.
  • Understanding of the relationship between federal health programs and state-level implementation.

How you'll work

Market Development at Agile Six is a team effort. You will own significant areas of strategy and pipeline, but you won't operate as an isolated salesperson. You'll work with company leadership, Market Development teammates, delivery teams, and organizational partners to bring the right expertise into opportunities at the right time.

Our strongest growth comes from work we understand and can deliver well. That means staying close to Delivery, sharing intelligence openly, and measuring success by the quality and impact of the work we win.

Employment & Compensation

Engagement: Full-time; open to W-2 employment or an initial contract-to-hire arrangement.
Compensation: Compensation will depend on the final level and engagement structure. For W-2 employment, Agile Six's current base salaries for the levels under consideration range from $182,767–$250,460. Contract compensation would be established separately based on the engagement structure.Location: US Remote. Preference will be given to candidates in the MD/N.VA/DC area.

Sixer Benefits

Our benefits are designed to reinforce our core values of Wholeness, Self Management and Inclusion. We respect that only you know what balance means for your life and season. While we offer support from coaches, we expect you to own your wholeness, show up for work whole, and go home to your family the same. You will be seen, heard and valued. We expect you to offer the same for your colleagues, be kind (not controlling), be caring (not directive) and ready to participate in a state of flow. We mean it when we say “We build better by putting people first”.

  • Self-managed work/life balance and flexibility
  • Competitive salary
  • Employee Stock Ownership (ESOP) for all employees!
  • 401(k) matching
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Employer paid short and long term disability insurance
  • Employer paid life insurance
  • Self-managed and generous paid time off
  • Paid federal holidays and two floating holidays
  • Paid parental leave
  • Self-managed professional development spending
  • Self-managed wellness days

Hiring practices

Agile Six is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any factor protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

Note: We participate in E-Verify. Upon hire, we will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. Unfortunately, we are unable to sponsor visas at this time.

If you need assistance or reasonable accommodation in applying for any of these positions, please reach out to . We want to ensure you have the ability to apply for any position at Agile Six.

Please read and respond to the application questions carefully. Interviews are conducted on a rolling basis until the position has been filled.

Opportunity:

We are currently hiring adjunct faculty to teach SPAC 520- Principles of Space Systems.

Course Description

Fundamental principles of space systems including spacecraft subsystems, satellite payloads, and space environment interactions.

Applicable Professional Certification

Project Management Professional (PMP)

Please note that ERAU policy requires that all adjuncts be physically located within the United States while working for the University, including during training. Presently, we are able to support work for new adjuncts from all U.S. states exceptCalifornia. ERAU does not support work from international locations with some limited exceptions for individuals who are residing and working from U.S. military bases.

If selected for this role, the candidate will be required to provide proof of stated qualifications.
